expected.title: Canonical equivalence of the tight coherent diagonal subdivisions of normally equivalent positively oriented polytopes
expected.author: Naruki Masuda; Hugh Thomas; Andy Tonks; Bruno Vallette
expected.difficulty_reason: The proposition compares two polytopes that are only normally equivalent, and its proof must first replace the definition of the diagonal by a normal-fan condition: for x in the relative interior of a face F and y in the relative interior of a face G, the pair (x,y) lies in im(triangle_P) exactly when no vector w with <v,w> > 0 lies in -N_P(F)^* cap N_P(G)^* (source lines 1134-1146). This rests on the polar-cone description of the normal cone of the face through y and on the orientation hypotheses on (P,v) and (Q,v), not on the face lattices alone. The step that cannot be done routinely is turning that membership test into a canonical combinatorial equivalence of the two tight coherent subdivisions, because the equivalence has to be induced by Phi x Phi on the face lattices (lines 1147-1148) rather than asserted from normal equivalence; standard normal-fan theory contains no diagonal-specific statement of this kind.

expected.title: Existence, uniqueness and invertibility of the transition map between positively oriented polytopes with equivalent diagonal subdivisions
expected.author: Naruki Masuda; Hugh Thomas; Andy Tonks; Bruno Vallette
expected.difficulty_reason: The proposition demands a map between two different positively oriented polytopes that simultaneously extends a prescribed vertex bijection and commutes with two different diagonal maps; the proof shows such a tr is forced to be beta_Q^(n) o tr^(2^n) o triangle_P^(n) (source line 1202), so the map has to be manufactured rather than read off. Existence is an induction on the dimension whose induction step needs the filtration P(n) together with cor:DIMENSION to know that the iterated diagonal of z in P(n) lies in the (d-1)-skeleton (lines 1213-1229). The part that cannot be done routinely is continuity at the main axis [bottom(P),top(P)]: it requires a dichotomy between non-dyadic and dyadic axis points and an explicit choice of n with diam Q < 2^n epsilon (lines 1232-1267), a quantitative argument that no standard polytope fact supplies.

expected.title: Monotonicity, positivity, edge direction and facet containment for the folding map of the associahedron
expected.author: Naruki Masuda; Hugh Thomas; Andy Tonks; Bruno Vallette
expected.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four properties of the folding map L that sends the vertices of the polytope P to the Boolean lattice: monotonicity along the lattice order, positivity of the scalar products with the coordinate vectors, the direction of the edges joining L-fibres, and the containment of every fibre in a facet (statement lines 1414-1425). The proof treats the four clauses separately, and the two that carry content are the third, where the edge vector between two neighbouring trees is computed explicitly as omega_i omega_{i+2} e_i on a single polytope K_omega, and the fourth, where an occurrence of the pattern (1,0) in the folding sequence produces the facet containing the fibre (proof lines 1434-1439). The second clause is dismissed by the author as straightforward from the definition of the vector; the first and fourth are argued in one sentence each but with the decisive observation stated. The proof is complete in the sense that every clause is addressed inside the span, so H2.

expected.title: The Loday realization of the associahedron: its hyperplane, its facets and its face lattice
expected.author: Naruki Masuda; Hugh Thomas; Andy Tonks; Bruno Vallette
expected.difficulty_reason: The proposition collects five properties of the weighted Loday realization K_omega of the associahedron: the hyperplane containing it, its description by half-spaces with equality exactly on decomposable trees, the fact that this hyperplane-and-half-space system cuts the polytope out, the identification of the face lattice with the lattice of planar trees, and the product decomposition of any face (statement lines 670-691). The proof's substance is in clauses (3) to (5): clause (3) requires showing that the equations defining a vertex have nested or disjoint intervals, which is done by deriving a strict inequality that contradicts the defining half-spaces (proof lines 699-731), clause (4) then reads the face lattice off the facet description of clause (2), and clause (5) exhibits the explicit isomorphism Theta putting a product of two smaller Loday realizations onto a facet (proof lines 738-753). Clauses (1) and (2) are dismissed by the author as straightforward from the definition, and both dismissals are kept verbatim in the counted span; they are not where the item's obligation lies, since the decisive statement is the combinatorial description of the polytope, which is proved. H2.
